title: The Silver Coin in the Palace Courtyard (HI)
summary: Akbar drops a silver coin on the floor to see which of his noble courtiers will stoop to pick it up. Birbal's reaction provides a lesson in self-respect. [HI]
full_text:
One afternoon in the Diwan-i-Khas, while testing the character of his courtiers, Emperor Akbar casually reached into his sash, pulled out a single silver rupee coin, and let it drop onto the polished marble floor.

*Clink!*

The coin rolled across the floor, coming to rest near a group of senior courtiers and ministers.

Instantly, three wealthy nawabs and two imperial scribes dove forward onto their hands and knees, scrambling across the floor, shoving each other aside, and pawing through the dust to grab the single silver coin!

A general snatched it triumphantly, dust coating his silk sleeves.

Meanwhile, Birbal stood quietly beside the Emperor, his hands folded, watching the undignified scramble with a calm, amused gaze.

Akbar smiled with disdain at the scrambling courtiers, then turned to Birbal: 'Birbal, you did not jump to pick up the silver coin. Do you despise money?'

Birbal replied with quiet grace:

'Sire, I respect honest wealth earned through labor and service. But a man who wears the robes of an imperial counselor should possess dignity worth more than thirty copper dams!

'When noblemen who govern provinces dive into the dirt to scramble over a single coin dropped from a monarch's hand, they show that they possess the minds of hungry street dogs, not the souls of statesmen!

'He who scrambles for petty crumbs will eventually sell his honor, his judgment, and his empire for a handful of silver. A true minister bows only to justice, never to dust.'

The scrambling courtiers stood up, red-faced with burning shame, brushing the dust from their knees.

Akbar commended Birbal, stating that character is measured not by how high a man climbs, but by how low he refuses to stoop.
